async_patterns.rule: Use async/await when steps are sequential and each depends on the previous result.

Use .then/.catch/.finally when the chain's resolved/rejected value is consumed only within the chain itself and no subsequent code depends on its outcome (e.g. teardown via `.finally` regardless of success/failure).
Violation: mixing paradigms inside a single `async` function — e.g. `await`-ing one call, then chaining `.then/.catch` off a later call instead of `await`-ing it.

component_declarations.rule: `function` declaration + named export. No `React.FC`, no default exports.
Ref-forwarding exception: `export const MyComponent = React.forwardRef<RefType, PropsType>(function MyComponent(...) {...})` — name the inner function for stack traces.
New JSX transform: omit `import * as React` unless the file references a type/value via the `React.` namespace (`React.RefObject`, `React.MouseEvent`, `React.CSSProperties`, `React.ReactNode`, etc.).
Return type `JSX.Element`; use `JSX.Element | null` when the component may render nothing (conditional renders).

guard_components.rule: A guard component controls access to a subtree: accepts a `Fallback` prop for the restricted state, renders `children` when the guard passes.
Fallback prop is always named `Fallback` (capital F).
Pass the fallback as an inline arrow at the call site: `Fallback={() => <MyFallback />}` — never inline JSX directly in the prop value.
Extract the fallback UI as a named `function` in the same file, following the same component-declaration rules (function declaration, `JSX.Element` return type, no `React.FC`).

http_response_patterns.rule: `json-http-request` defines `ResultOf<T>`: `{ Success: boolean; ErrorMessage: string | null; Data: T | null }`.
`JsonHttpRequest.PostResult()`/`GetResult()` unwrap `Data` and return it directly (not the envelope).
When `PostResult`/`GetResult` returns `null` (i.e. `Success: false`), callers must check for null and surface `ErrorMessage` to the user or throw.
Custom response types (not using `PostResult`/`GetResult`) may deviate from `ResultOf`; document the shape in the API file's interface.

state_and_data.rule: Core business logic lives in a class with `Observable`/`ObservableList` properties (`@residualeffect/reactor`), kept testable outside React.
Business/shared state: `@residualeffect/reactor` (`Observable`, `ObservableArray`, `ObservableObject`) inside service classes. Never `useState` outside local UI state.

Decision rule for `React.useState`: only for state that is purely presentational with no domain dependencies. If state is derived from domain data, affects domain data, or needs independent testing, it belongs in a service class.
Subscribe to `Observable`/`ObservableList` via `useObservable` (`@residualeffect/rereactor`); the component re-renders only when the observed value changes.
Subscribe via `@residualeffect/rereactor`'s `useObservable` hook. Exception: ui-rewards hand-rolls equivalent.
`useObservable` on an `ObservableList` returns the current array; a new array reference is emitted on every mutation, so no extra memoization is needed for correct re-rendering.
Form validation: `ValidatableFieldOf<T>` Observable with `Computed` derivations (`IsValid`, `ValidationMessage`, `HasChanged`, `CanSave`). (3 SPAs only; ui-rewards excludes.)
Data fetch: `@webmdhs/json-http-request` promise-based `Get`/`Post`/`Result`. Exception: ui-rewards uses callback-chained `HttpProxy` (`Success()`/`Failure()`).
Response envelopes: Three competing shapes—discriminated union (`SuccessValidationResultOf<T>`), library `Result` extension, flat `ResultOf<T>`. Check which before writing response handlers.

string_checks.rule: Use `HasString` (`@webmdhs/general-data-structures`) for non-empty string guards, not manual null/length checks (`str != null && str.length > 0`, `!!str`, `str?.length > 0`, `str !== ""`, etc.).
When suggesting `HasString`, include the import `import { HasString } from "@webmdhs/general-data-structures";` if not already present.

directory_structure.rule: Replace the loose global wildcard (`"paths": { "*": ["*"] }`) with a scoped prefix alias (e.g. `"@/*": ["./src/client/*"]`) under `moduleResolution: "Bundler"`. Mirror the same prefix in Webpack `resolve.alias` so runtime resolution matches TypeScript. This prevents TS from crawling `node_modules`, config dirs, and build artifacts during module resolution.
Isolate Node server in `server/` point `package.json` `main` at it.

naming_conventions.rule: Generic type params: T-prefixed PascalCase (`TDataPoint`, `ValidatableFieldOf<T>`), never bare letters.
Public methods/properties: PascalCase (.NET-style), even in TS/TSX.
Services: `<Feature>Service` class name. Singleton services expose static `Instance` getter (ui-admin-infrastructure, ui-rewards).

component_architecture.rule: Prefer function declarations with explicit return types over `React.FC` arrows.
Service classes hold business logic; components are purely presentational. Decoupled singleton, view-data-shaper, service-locator, or factory as role.
`RouterLinkTo` factory: `export default function RouterLinkTo(to: string): React.ElementType { … }` — adapts MUI `component` prop to react-router.
Type-dispatch factory: shared interface `IDataPointTypeService` with per-type implementers, facade resolver at runtime.
Use Builder pattern for shaped domain objects.
Context + `useX` hook: co-locate in same file. Class holds state/logic; hook wraps Observable subscription.
Slot props: generic table accepts per-column components (`HeaderComponent`, `DataComponent`).

styling_strategy.rule: Use `sx` prop with `SystemStyleObject<Theme>` on MUI v6/v7. Pattern: `const Styles = (_theme: Theme): SystemStyleObject<Theme> => ({…})`.
Theme: shared internal WebMD base package, not vanilla MUI/Material-UI defaults. ui-rewards uses `@webmdhs/jss-theme` (v4); others use `@webmdhs/mui-theme` (v6/v7).
When multiple React versions share a page, pair `ScopedCssBaseline` with an Emotion `CacheProvider` to isolate styles and avoid cross-version bleed.
Use `GlobalStyles` for global CSS overrides that cannot be scoped.
Per-icon imports using `Rounded` variant; MUI components via default imports, not barrel. Theme merge via `deepmerge` from `@mui/utils`.
Use TypeScript module augmentation to declare custom MUI component variants.

language_idioms.rule: Use `HasString` from `@webmdhs/general-data-structures` for string-presence checks instead of manual null/length checks.

technical_debt.critical: Material-UI v4 vs. v6/v7 elsewhere. Root cause cascades: JSS vs `sx` styling, `@webmdhs/jss-theme` vs `@webmdhs/mui-theme`, hand-rolled `HttpProxy`/`useObservable` instead of shared packages. v4→v6/v7 migration unlocks cross-app code sharing.
technical_debt.high: HTTP paradigm split: promise-based `@webmdhs/json-http-request` (3 SPAs) vs. callback-based `HttpProxy`. Treat as real migration cost when moving code.
technical_debt.medium: `useObservable` duplicated locally instead of using `@residualeffect/rereactor`. Identical behavior, independent maintenance, drift risk.
Response envelope shapes inconsistent across group. Code touching >1 SPA's API layer must verify shape first.

crux_bot_rules.universal_baseline: • Absolute-path imports via a scoped prefix alias (e.g. `@/*`) in tsconfig `paths` under `moduleResolution: "Bundler"`, mirrored in Webpack `resolve.alias`. • Business state via `@residualeffect/reactor` in service classes, never `useState` for shared state. • Custom MUI/Material-UI theme from shared internal WebMD package. • `<Feature>Service` class for business/view logic, decoupled from presentational components.
